Featured.title: Featured
Featured.paragraph1: I've developed a mobile app for tracking and rating readings. Each user can search for or scan a book, rate it, leave a comment, manage their reading status, and much more !
Featured.paragraph2: The unique feature of this app is that your profile page reflects your reading habits. You can create different bookshelves, add as many books as you want, and add a description.
Featured.paragraph3: You can arrange the bookshelves however you like on your profile, which also displays your reading goal and what you're currently reading. All the information you need to let your friends know your current reading mood !

Projects.descTitle: A few <important>digital objects</important> crafted with care

my-shelf.name: MyShelf
my-shelf.description: A personal bookshelf to track and share your reading.
longDescription: With this project, I tried to bring together my two passions: reading and code. I was missing a way to track the books I'd read and everything that goes with my everyday life as a reader.
I first turned to Goodreads, StoryGraph and Babelio, but none of them suited me or had features that really matched what I needed.

So I decided to build my own app! Simple reading tracking, an efficient search, easy reviews and ratings. It also works as an index of my reading and, above all, lets me customise my profile in depth and share it with anyone.
my-shelf.tagline: A reading tracker, made by a reader.
technical: Everything lives in a Turborepo monorepo run with Bun: the Expo mobile app, the Next.js website, an admin and the NestJS API. Shared packages hold the types, validation and API clients, so mobile and web speak the same language as the server.

Book records combine ISBNdb, Open Library and the BnF to cover as many editions as possible. PostgreSQL, Prisma and Redis handle the data, Cloudflare R2 the images, and Sentry and Grafana tell me when something breaks.

noomi.name: Noomi
noomi.description: A personality test that brings a little companion to life.
longDescription: Noomi is a playful self-discovery tool. It starts with a twenty-question quiz inspired by the Big Five, the most studied personality model. The answers sketch a portrait, and that portrait takes the shape of a unique creature: your Noomi.

It then grows with you. One question a day refines the portrait, “My weather” keeps track of your mood, and each habit grows a plant in its garden. Nothing is lost on days when you do nothing: the idea is to move at your own pace, not to feel guilty.
It isn't a diagnosis, and the app says so clearly. It's a light way to know yourself better, with a companion that makes you want to come back.
highlights: 20-question quiz inspired by the Big Five
A unique creature generated from your portrait
One question a day to refine that portrait
“My weather”: the day as a timeline, the week as a forecast, the month as a calendar
A garden that grows with your habits, with nothing lost on days off
noomi.tagline: A personality test that becomes a companion.
technical: The heart of the project is a framework-free TypeScript package: the quiz, the scoring and the creature generator are written as pure functions. Web, mobile and API import the same code, so they all produce the same Noomi.

No creature is drawn by hand. Each personality trait sets an organ, and a seed makes the drawing unique and reproducible. Rendering is locked by tests on 624 reference SVGs, so an update never changes someone's Noomi.
Around that: Expo and React Native for the app, Next.js for the website, NestJS with Better Auth, Prisma and PostgreSQL for the API, all in a Turborepo monorepo.

dependant-tv.name: Dependant.tv
dependant-tv.description: The website of the production company Dependant, built to put their films and photos front and centre.
longDescription: Dependant is a production company: commercials, music videos, photography. For them the website is a showreel, so the images had to come before everything else.
Projects are sorted by type, with dedicated pages for directors and photographers. Films start quickly without weighing the pages down, and the site exists in French and English.
The team is autonomous: they add a project, a director or a photographer and set the order of the lists from their CMS, without going through me.
highlights: Strapi CMS with video upload from the admin
dependant-tv.tagline: A production company's website, where the films come first.
technical: Next.js with next-intl for the two languages, Mux to stream the videos and GSAP for the animations.

The CMS is a Strapi hosted on a VPS: PostgreSQL for the content, S3 storage for the files and a Mux plugin to upload videos from the admin. Each environment has its own process, database and files, so everything can be checked before going live.

ali-bensaali-production.name: Ali Bensaali Production
ali-bensaali-production.description: The portfolio of Ali Bensaali, an independent director and cinematographer, built around his two crafts.
longDescription: Ali Bensaali is an independent director and cinematographer. He needed a website that shows his work quickly and at full size, without needing me for every new film.
The site is built around his two crafts, with one entry for directing and one for cinematography. Films start right away and pages stay light despite the amount of video.
highlights: Content managed by Ali from Contentful
ali-bensaali-production.tagline: A director's portfolio, all in images.
technical: Next.js for the website, GSAP for motion and Mux for the videos. Images go through Cloudinary, which serves the right format for each screen.
Contentful acts as the back office: Ali adds his projects himself, without touching the code.

labcom-optimaa.name: Labcom Optimaa
labcom-optimaa.description: The website of LabCom OPTIMAA, a joint lab between Z3DLAB and the CNRS's LSPM on additive manufacturing.
longDescription: OPTIMAA is a joint laboratory between the company Z3DLAB and the LSPM, a CNRS lab. It works on metal alloys made through additive manufacturing.
The website presents the project, the team and the news, and it moves at the pace of research: the researchers had to be able to publish by themselves, sometimes every day.
So I set up an admin dashboard on Strapi for the news, and a bilingual website designed to stay readable on a very technical subject.
labcom-optimaa.tagline: The showcase of a joint lab between industry and research.
technical: Next.js and next-intl for the website, Strapi with PostgreSQL for the content.
A CI/CD pipeline deploys every update automatically, so the website stays current without any intervention.

cocoa-bio.name: Cocoa bio
cocoa-bio.description: The website of the CoCoA-bio research project, on additive manufacturing of metal bio-implants.
longDescription: CoCoA-bio is a research project on additive manufacturing of metal bio-implants, run with Z3DLAB, LSPM, BIOCIS, ITODYS and URB2i.

The website follows the project over time: summary, goals, results, publications, outlook and partners. The challenge was to make a very technical subject readable, with clear pages and just enough animation.
highlights: Complete presentation of a research project
cocoa-bio.tagline: A research project on metal bio-implants, presented online.
technical: Next.js and next-intl for the two languages, GSAP for scroll animations.
The content rarely changes, so no CMS: fast, well-ranked pages.

interlude-decors.name: Interlude Decors
interlude-decors.description: The portfolio of Agathe Roger, who creates sets, models and 3D modelling.
longDescription: Agathe Roger creates sets, models and 3D modelling. Her work is very visual and spans several crafts, so the website had to show everything without getting lost.
The site is organised by field: sets, models, stands and photography, with a downloadable résumé. Agathe adds her work herself from Contentful.
highlights: Four fields: sets, models, stands, photography
Content managed by Agathe from Contentful
interlude-decors.tagline: The online portfolio of a set designer.
technical: Next.js and Tailwind for the website, GSAP and Swiper for the galleries.
Contentful for the content and Cloudinary for the images, served at the right size for each screen.

About.title: About me
About.paragraph1: I started coding out of curiosity, to understand how the websites I visited were made. Very quickly, the desire to build took precedence over the desire to consume, and it has never left me since.
About.paragraph2: The front end is my playground, but I'm involved in the entire chain: back end, data, infrastructure.
About.paragraph3: Outside of the screen, I read a lot. Philosophy, essays, fiction. That's what motivated me to create MyShelf, a tool for my reading, not a social network.
